findings.title: The copy that sells the product is the faintest thing on the page

location.description: the lead paragraph, the three card descriptions and the footer text

findings.viewer_experience: Low-vision readers and anyone in bright light lose the body copy, and everyone else treats it as fine print and skips it. It is the only place the page names studios, late-payment follow-up and the shared accountant link.
findings.target: contrast of at least 4.5:1 (something near #595959 or darker)
findings.fix_direction: Darken the body text to at least 4.5:1. Keep the light grey only for the footer, if anywhere.

closed_when.check: contrast of p.lead, div.cards > div.card > p in the desktop viewport is 4.5 or more

findings.title: Two equal primary buttons give no hint which action the page wants

location.description: the 'Start free trial' and 'Book a demo' buttons

findings.viewer_experience: The visitor has to choose between two identical filled blue buttons with no hint which one the page wants.
findings.target: one high-emphasis action per view: 'Start free trial' filled, 'Book a demo' outlined or text
findings.fix_direction: Keep 'Start free trial' filled and make 'Book a demo' an outlined or text button. Better still, name what the trial button does, e.g. 'Send your first invoice free'.

jev.title: Secondary actions are styled as strongly as the primary one

closed_when.check: A fresh critic sees one filled primary button and the other action styled clearly weaker

findings.title: The headline could be anyone's, and the real reason to buy is buried in a grey paragraph

location.description: the headline and the lead paragraph under it

findings.viewer_experience: The visitor can't tell what is different here, so nothing pushes them to act.

current.value: headline 'Send invoices in minutes, not hours'; audience and advantage only in sentences three and four of the lead

findings.target: the audience and the sharpest benefit in the headline or a short subhead; the paragraph cut to one or two sentences
findings.fix_direction: Put the audience and the sharpest benefit in the headline or a short subhead, for example open with the pain of late payments ('Stop chasing clients for late payments') rather than speed. Then cut the paragraph to one or two sentences.

closed_when.check: A fresh critic can tell from the headline or subhead who the product is for and why it is different

findings.title: Multi-line paragraphs are centred, and the lead runs too long a line

location.description: the 4-line lead paragraph and the card descriptions

findings.viewer_experience: Each line starts somewhere different, so the eye has to hunt for the start of the next one.
findings.target: multi-line text flush left; lead at no more than about 70 characters per line (45–75 range)
findings.fix_direction: Set multi-line text flush left. If you keep a centred hero, cut the lead to one or two short lines at no more than about 70 characters, and left-align the card text.
findings.source: Tschichold, The New Typography; Bringhurst 2.1.2 and 2.1.3

jev.title: A paragraph is centered or right-aligned

closed_when.check: characters_per_line of p.lead in the desktop viewport is 75 or less, and the multi-line paragraphs are left-aligned in the new image

findings.title: The heavy black rules and card borders are the strongest marks on the page

location.description: the full-width rules under the header and above the footer, and the outlines around each card

findings.viewer_experience: They carry more visual weight than the card titles or the text inside them, so the page reads as wireframe scaffolding.

current.value: near-black rules and card outlines heavier than the content

findings.target: rules and borders removed or replaced by space or a pale tint, so the content sets the weight
findings.fix_direction: Remove the rules and borders, or swap them for space or a pale tint.
findings.source: Lupton, Thinking with Type; Tufte on non-data ink

closed_when.check: A fresh critic sees no rule or border heavier than the content it frames

findings.title: The section title looks like body text

location.description: the section title 'Why studios use Quillfern'

findings.viewer_experience: It is 16 px regular, the same as body text, so it doesn't read as a heading.
findings.target: a size step or bold weight above body text
findings.fix_direction: Give it a size step or bold weight.

closed_when.check: font_size of p.section-title in the desktop viewport is above 16, or font_weight is 600 or more

findings.title: The heading promises reasons but the cards name feature categories

location.description: the heading 'Why studios use Quillfern' and the card titles Invoices, Reminders, Reports

findings.viewer_experience: The cards are named feature categories, not reasons, so the heading doesn't match what follows.

current.value: heading 'Why studios use Quillfern' over cards titled Invoices, Reminders, Reports

findings.target: heading and card titles that agree
findings.fix_direction: Rename the heading ('What Quillfern does') or rewrite the card titles as outcomes ('Get paid without chasing').

closed_when.check: A fresh critic sees a heading that names what the cards under it are

findings.title: Card 1 ends with 'PDF.' alone on its last line

location.description: the description in the Invoices card

findings.viewer_experience: A single word alone on the last line looks like a loose end.

closed_when.check: A fresh critic sees no single word alone on the last line of the Invoices card text

findings.title: Nothing in the navigation marks the current page

location.description: the navigation links Home / Features / Pricing / Help

findings.viewer_experience: Home, Features, Pricing and Help all look the same, so the visitor can't tell where they are.
findings.target: the current item carries one cue, such as bold weight or an underline
findings.fix_direction: Give the current item one cue, such as bold weight or an underline.

jev.title: The navigation menu does not mark the current page

closed_when.check: A fresh critic sees one nav item marked as the current page

findings.title: On the phone the page scrolls sideways and the cards are squeezed

location.description: the whole page in the phone viewport, and the three cards in particular

findings.viewer_experience: The page scrolls sideways, and the side-by-side cards squeeze descriptions to 6–10 characters per line.

current.value: page 428 px wide in a 390 px viewport; 6–10 characters per line in the card text

findings.target: no sideways scroll; cards stacked in one column below about 600 px
findings.fix_direction: Stack the cards in one column below about 600 px.

closed_when.check: page_width equals width (390) in the phone viewport, and characters_per_line of div.card > p in the phone viewport is 45 or more
